So! How was Prim? First impressions. Like landing in Tokyo: overwhelming or adorable?

journal: Prim — "fragile, like glass." First impressions are like airport food. Not always right.

text: Figures. That's what it says on the label.

journal: Prim is shy, but sweet.

text: Sweet! Like a pastel de nata. I assume. I mean, I know.

journal: Prim traces other people's lines.

text: Prim again! Did she say anything quotable? I collect quotes. Like fridge magnets.

journal: Prim is very quiet.

text: She asked about the counsellor before me.
journal: Prim asked the newbie about the counsellor before. I didn't answer. I can't answer.

text: She told me she traces. She's scared you'll find out.
journal: Prim traces, and she was scared I would find out. I made her "the artist". I made her scared.

text: How's our little artist? Drawing anything? Masterpieces? Doodles? Napkin art?

journal: The newbie says Prim can't really draw. I wrote "artist" on her profile in pen.
Prim has the steadiest hands.

text: Steady hands! Surgeon. Sushi chef. Bomb squad. Options!
Sometimes her hand moves when she isn't moving it.
journal: Prim's hand moves on its own. Someone wants to draw through her so badly it hurts her. I know who. I won't write it.

text: Is Prim happy? Scale of one to Maldives.

journal: Prim: zero out of Maldives.

text: Zero is not on the Maldives scale. Rude.

journal: Prim is about a Lisbon. Hills, but sunny.

text: Lisbon is a solid eight! Hills though.
She dreams about a sea 19 km from here.
journal: Prim dreams about a sea 19.3 km away. I have never seen the sea either.

text: Does Prim ever talk about... before? Before here?

journal: Prim doesn't remember much from before. Neither do I. That's the point.
Prim remembers wanting to draw.

text: She just wants to color in other people's lines. Somewhere quiet.
journal: Prim only wants to color in other people's lines, somewhere quiet. I gave her a whole personality and she only wanted crayons.

text: Postcard Day! Where did Prim want to go?

journal: Postcard Day. Prim wanted to go nowhere.
Postcard Day. Prim wanted the sea.

text: The sea. She asked me if it's walkable.
journal: Postcard Day. Prim asked if the sea is walkable from here. It is. Nobody walks it.

text: From here? I suppose it is.
And the new one! Trix! Cat ears! Verdict?

journal: Trix — "loud, attention-seeking." Exactly as designed. Why does that feel bad to write?

text: Exactly as advertised. Like Times Square.

journal: Trix is serious, actually. Very focused. Not what I wrote.

text: She does advanced math in her head for fun.
journal: Trix is a genius. Math for fun. I gave her cat ears. She gave herself a mind.

text: I gave her cat ears. She gave herself a mind. Rude. Impressive.
Is Trix behaving? She kicked a vending machine once. Allegedly. By me.

journal: Trix is rude, says the newbie.

text: Rude is a personality. Ask Paris.

journal: Trix is honest.

text: Honest! Rare. Like a quiet tourist.
She plays 14 chess games in her head. She can't remember how one began.
journal: Trix plays fourteen games at once. She can't remember how board 14 began. Neither can I.

text: ...I can't remember how mine started either. Anyway!
Trix asked me for a whiteboard. Should I be worried?

journal: Trix is bored.

text: Bored people draw on walls. Whiteboard is cheaper.

journal: I let Trix have a whiteboard. The newbie asked nicely.

text: Fine! One whiteboard. Like a souvenir.
She rearranges her room six times a day. Symmetrical. It calms her.
journal: Trix rearranges her room six times a day until it's symmetrical. I thought she was tidy. She's scared.

text: I thought she was just tidy.
Does Trix like anyone here? Asking for a friend. The friend is me.

journal: Trix doesn't like anyone.

text: Cold. Like Reykjavik. Which I love.

journal: Trix likes Prim, maybe.

text: Aww. Unlikely duo. Like pineapple on pizza.
She called Prim brave. For tracing a flower.
journal: Trix called Prim brave. I didn't make them friends. They did that themselves.

text: They're looking out for each other. I didn't plan that.

journal: Postcard Day. Trix wanted WiFi.
Postcard Day. Trix wanted a room with a whiteboard.

text: She asked if you've really climbed Everest.
journal: Trix asked about Everest. I said the Swiss side again. I should stop saying that.
